title: Verification of the accuracy of existing technical documentation
description: Verification is necessary at three key stages of the project’s life:

blocks.text: Main reasons for verifying technical documentation:

items: Safety and compliance with standards: Verification ensures that the project meets current industry standards, technical specifications, fire safety regulations and safety requirements (e.g. CE).

Avoiding errors and saving costs: Checking the documentation before construction allows detection of inconsistencies, ambiguities, or errors, thereby preventing costly rectifications during the construction phase.
Completeness and consistency: Ensuring that all elements of the design (structural, services) fit together and there are no clashes.
Formal and legal requirements: Verification is essential for obtaining permits and serves as the basis for regulatory bodies, engineers, and operators.
Optimisation: It allows for the introduction of alternative changes that may reduce investment costs.

blocks.text: At what stages do we check projects?
Verification is necessary at three key stages of the project’s life:

items: Before the start of the project (to eliminate design errors while still on paper).
During implementation (as a detailed verification of as-built documentation).

Before any modernisation (to ensure that the planned reconstruction makes sense and is completely safe).Before any modernisation (to ensure that the planned reconstruction makes sense and is completely safe).
